name: Waaree Energies Ltd
title: Waaree Energies Ltd - 544277 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).
Imported cell about USD0.04-0.045/W versus Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W; DCR market price about USD0.12-0.13/W.
US market had about six months of installation lull due to tariff uncertainty; management reports recent order and enquiry pickup, including data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion timeline for 10 GW cell and wafer and battery capacity over FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 28 GW modules, 15.4 GW cells, 4 GW inverters and 20 GVA transformers by FY27-end; FY28 to see about 16-18 GW modules and about 10 GW cell output. The 10 GW Indian cell facility adds from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did module gross margin fall, and what are the recovery levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower IRA realisation in Q1 because US dispatches came from OEM manufacturing; delayed non-DCR offtake; softer exports. Levers are DCR cell output, US local scaling, exports from August, and non-DCR offtake over the six-month window.

qa_highlights.question: How are US export and US local manufacturing margins structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports from India earn about USD0.04-0.05/W EBITDA. US local manufacturing nets about USD0.055-0.06/W after expenses, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W. Management guides total US local realisation and EBITDA at USD0.07-0.08/W, helped by a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower-cost import option for cells compared with domestic manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported cell is about USD0.04-0.045/W against Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W and DCR market price of USD0.12-0.13/W.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS volume and earnings outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5.15 GWh container line is live and order book is building. The 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27. FEOC-compliant cell realisations are about 25-30% above Chinese pricing, with non-FEOC at USD75-80/kWh versus Chinese USD50-55/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholders approved about INR10,000 crore of fundraising including equity. Management says FY27 EBITDA is broadly sufficient to fund the capex and it will wait for the right market window. Balance capex is about INR22,000 crore over three years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation and a lower IRA realisation mix in Q1; watch whether 18.2% operating EBITDA margin recovers toward the FY27 guidance band.
Second-half weighted order book and inventory build; utilisation of India modules around 50% annualised in Q1 versus a 70-75% target for Q3-Q4.
Timing of the 10 GW Indian cell commissioning (targeted by December) and ALMM-II extension window; the non-DCR offtake ramp is unconfirmed.
US export clearance delays and the start of US local line output from August; US IRA incentive monetisation timing.
Capex execution across INR31,500 crore programme and the glass capex decision, with an update promised in about one quarter.
Pending QIP and funding plan; BESS Make-in-India incentive is not yet announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, order book and capacity milestones, but candid about Q1 margin and dispatch shortfalls. Management repeatedly tied recovery to specific dated levers and reaffirmed guidance. Responses on glass capex, BESS incentives and QIP timing were less specific.
key_quotes: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.
Our cell-to-module integration ratio is going to rise from roughly around 20% currently to around 65% in next two to three quarters, close to a threefold increase.
It is on this trend that we affirm and reaffirm our 2027 operating EBITDA guidance, what we have stated in our last call.
